one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls in the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29 window: Q4 FY26 results (Aug 25) and Investor Day (Sep 17, guidance reaffirmed) are behind us, and Q1 FY27 results normally come in late November. The Oct 16 dividend payment is immaterial. What can move it is unscheduled: more frontier-lab consumer finance/tax launches (the stock has repeatedly sold off on OpenAI/ChatGPT finance headlines), further sell-side cuts (24 down vs 5 up EPS revisions in 30 days), and the pending securities class action. Momentum is strongly negative (-23% in a month, near the $252.84 52-week low), but the stock is also oversold at ~11.6x FY27 EPS, so the two short-horizon effects roughly cancel. I use a near-symmetric lognormal around $268 with ~14% monthly vol (50%/3.5) and a very slight downward tilt for momentum and headline risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of a skeptic-haircut P/E (FY28 SBC-inclusive EPS $24.5 x 12.5x = $306), an SBC-adjusted FCF yield of 7.5% on normalized ~$5.6B FCF (~$285), and a Goldman-style 15x FY27 GAAP EPS of $20.24 (~$304), weighted 0.40/0.35/0.25.

bear.story: The Jan-Apr 2027 tax season confirms structural erosion: DIY units fall again (already -2% in FY26), ARPC cuts don't buy share, AI-native/free filers take the low end, TurboTax revenue declines, and FY28 guidance (Aug 2027) is mid-single-digit growth. Mailchimp impairment, Credit Karma cyclical slowdown and loan-book losses add noise. ~9x on ~$20 EPS.

base.story: Company roughly hits FY27 guide (9-10% revenue, ~$23 EPS); TurboTax flat-to-slightly-up, QuickBooks/GBS 13-14% growth carries the story; buybacks continue at $5B+/yr. Multiple stays depressed (~12-13x NTM) because the AI overhang does not resolve in one season.

bull.story: Tax season shows TurboTax Live/assisted growth and customer re-acceleration, AI partnerships (OpenAI, Anthropic channel) look like distribution rather than disintermediation; multiple re-rates toward 17x on ~$25 EPS, toward the ~$405 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: Around $205 (~9x FY27 EPS incl. SBC, ~10% SBC-adjusted FCF yield) the market would be pricing an outright decline in earnings, not just deceleration. A move there would most likely mean either a failed tax season (TurboTax units/revenue down materially in the May 2027 update) or GBS/QuickBooks growth breaking below ~10%, i.e. AI disruption spreading from consumer tax to small-business accounting, which would invalidate the base case.

How much the depressed multiple (~11.6x) already prices in; buybacks at these prices boost EPS
reasoning: Facts: FY26 revenue $21.4B (+14%), GAAP EPS $16.46. FY27 guide is 9-10% revenue, TurboTax only +2-3% (management is deliberately cutting DIY ARPC because 'price is now the number one reason customers leave'), Mailchimp -1% to 0%, and non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12, which now includes $5.81 of SBC. At $268 the stock is ~11.6x FY27 EPS and ~13x GAAP, with 267M shares (~$72B market cap) and near-zero net debt (debt $7.7B, cash $7.2B). The bear evidence from my lane is real but mostly already in the price: Goldman went to Sell with a $276 target (AI can prepare a return for ~$0.12 vs ~$162 TurboTax ARPC; TurboTax revenue ~18% below FY25 by 2030 if 20% of filers switch); TD Cowen (Hold, $304) expects the catalyst path to skew negative until the May 2027 tax-season readout; JPMorgan and Wolfe downgraded; two securities class actions filed (Jul/Aug 2026) over TurboTax competitive disclosures; 17% workforce cut; the CEO sold $26.6M in January at ~$650 under a 10b5-1 plan and holds few shares directly; TurboTax units fell 2% in FY26. Accounting check: FY26 OCF of $8.8B is inflated by a $1.28B deferred-tax add-back tied to OBBBA R&D expensing and the company funds a growing lending book; SBC-adjusted normalized FCF is ~$5.3B, a ~7.4% yield, which is cheap for a business still growing high single digits in total. Credit is not a stress point: investment-grade, $1.75B notes issued in June 2026 to prefund FY27 maturities, $2.2B revolver undrawn, covenants met. I found no activist short report. My fair value blends three methods at ~$298, about 11% above spot. Scenario mean ~$300 (bear $180/25%, base $300/50%, bull $420/25%). For the ladder I use a lognormal with median ~$285 and sigma ~0.42 (below the 50% realized vol, which was inflated by a one-off de-rating, but with a slightly fatter left tail for a failed tax season). The result: P(>= spot) ~0.555, and P(>= $402, the consensus target) only ~0.2, because the key catalyst (the 2027 tax season) could go either way and the sell-side is still cutting. Research was focused (~14 queries); X/Twitter and prediction markets were not checked; Benzinga blocked fetching.
